---
title: "Drought"
subtitle: "Option 3 · The early warning for a short grass year"
---

```{python}
#| output: asis
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from sitekit import show
from sitekit.config import load_site
print(show.preview_banner())
ok = show.available("drought")
counties = load_site()["drought_area_label"]
if ok:
    d = show.drought_weekly()
    d["in_drought"] = d[["d1", "d2", "d3", "d4"]].sum(axis=1)
    last = d.iloc[-1]
    prior = d[d.date <= last.date - pd.Timedelta(days=365)]
    yr_ago = prior.iloc[-1] if len(prior) else last
    share_years = (d.groupby(d.date.dt.year)["in_drought"].mean() >= 50).sum()
    print(f"""::: {{.lead}}
On {last.date:%B} {last.date.day}, {last.date.year}, **an average of {last.in_drought:.0f}% across {counties}** was in moderate or worse drought, compared with {yr_ago.in_drought:.0f}% a year earlier.
:::
""")
else:
    print(show.missing_note("drought"))
```

The U.S. Drought Monitor is a weekly national map built by drought scientists from rain, soil moisture, streamflow, and local reports. Because grass responds to rain with a lag, drought conditions in spring are one of the best early signs of a short forage year.

## Every week since 2000

```{python}
if ok:
    fig = go.Figure()
    for k in ["d4", "d3", "d2", "d1", "d0"]:
        fig.add_scatter(x=d.date, y=d[k], stackgroup="one", mode="none", name=show.DROUGHT_LABEL[k],
                        fillcolor=show.DROUGHT[k], hovertemplate="%{x|%b %d, %Y}: %{y:.0f}%<extra>" + show.DROUGHT_LABEL[k] + "</extra>")
    fig.update_layout(yaxis=dict(title="Mean county area share (%)", range=[0, 100]),
                      legend=dict(traceorder="reversed"))
    show.show(fig, 400)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if ok:
    print(f"""Counties receive equal weight; this is not an area-weighted regional percentage. Colors stack up to the mean county share across {counties} in each drought category that week. In {share_years} of the {d.date.dt.year.nunique()} years shown, the mean county area share exceeded 50% in drought on average.""")
```

## The last twelve months

```{python}
if ok:
    recent = d[d.date >= last.date - pd.Timedelta(days=365)]
    fig = go.Figure()
    for k in ["d4", "d3", "d2", "d1", "d0"]:
        fig.add_bar(x=recent.date, y=recent[k], name=show.DROUGHT_LABEL[k], marker_color=show.DROUGHT[k],
                    hovertemplate="%{x|%b %d}: %{y:.0f}%<extra>" + show.DROUGHT_LABEL[k] + "</extra>")
    fig.update_layout(barmode="stack", bargap=0.05, yaxis=dict(title="Mean county area share (%)", range=[0, 100]),
                      legend=dict(traceorder="reversed"))
    show.show(fig, 320)
```

## What it tells a range manager

- **Whether to expect a short grass year** before the grass shows it.
- **When to start drought plans:** lining up hay, moving animals, or reducing numbers early, while prices and options are better.
- **A record for drought relief programs**, which often use Drought Monitor categories to decide who qualifies.
